bindings.label: Patient presented with a 6-hour history of dizziness, vomiting and unstable walking

Patient is a 36-year-old male with no smoking history, no sedentary lifestyle (BMI 24.2), no special medical history, no hypertension, diabetes, coronary heart disease, and no family history of stroke
Patient reported having a large rotation range of the head and neck before onset
Physical examination: patient was conscious with clear speech; left finger-nose test and heel-knee-tibia test were slightly inaccurate; Romberg sign positive; NIHSS score 1 point
Cerebrospinal fluid pressure was 270mmH2O and cerebrospinal fluid protein was 53mg/dl
MRI shows multiple acute infarcts in left thalamus, occipital lobe, and cerebellum
CTA shows fenestration of the left vertebral artery
Cardiac and autoimmune workups are negative
Posterior circulation stroke due to arteriopathic/embolic mechanism
Echocardiography and Holter monitoring show no abnormalities
CTA shows fenestration of the left vertebral artery at the V2-V3 segment
